defect: The new inherited-member walk delegates base discovery to cpp_direct_base_types, which prefers CodeUnit.signature() over source text. For C++ class templates, that identity signature is only the template parameter head, not the class declaration or its base clause. Splitting that metadata on a colon therefore loses the actual base and the new inherited-member lookup returns no definition for an otherwise ordinary base member.
defect_check: confirmed: a template-derived class has a nonempty identity signature containing only its template parameters, so cpp_direct_base_types does not read the class source and returns no base for the ordinary <class T> head.
fact: C++ class CodeUnits receive scope.template_signature as their identity signature (src/analyzer/cpp/declarations.rs:317-323), and that value contains only the template parameter head (src/analyzer/cpp/declarations.rs:1317-1331), excluding the class base clause.
query: What values reach CodeUnit::signature for class-template owners passed to cpp_direct_base_types, and do those values contain the class base clause?
other_facts: The template walk assigns the head to template_scope.template_signature at src/analyzer/cpp/declarations.rs:206-208.
cpp_direct_base_types prefers unit.signature() over analyzer.get_source and then requires a colon: src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:3211-3224.
The newly added inherited-member search invokes that existing helper at src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:3023.
The separately stored rendered signature at src/analyzer/cpp/declarations.rs:336-338 is distinct from CodeUnit::signature, which returns the identity field at src/analyzer/model.rs:355-356.
evidence: At intro 9c367d3f2eb0, the diff adds the inherited walk but does not modify cpp_direct_base_types (src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:3205-3224), the class signature producer (src/analyzer/cpp/declarations.rs:317-338), or cpp_template_signature (1317-1331). Following the identity value from the unchanged producer explains why a resolved template owner loses its inheritance edge.

defect: The new C# default candidate-file routing reduces each source file to one namespace via namespace_of_file, then admits unqualified type references only against that namespace. A valid reference under a later namespace block in the same file is omitted when its declaration is in another file, so the usage scanner never sees that reference.
defect_check: confirmed: referencing_files_of excludes an unqualified reference in a namespace other than the single namespace selected for its file. For usage scanning, place the consumer outside the defining file directory so directory-sibling candidates do not mask the omission.
fact: namespace_of_file selects only one nonempty namespace (src/analyzer/csharp_analyzer.rs:150-159), and referencing_files_of requires that single namespace to match before accepting bare type identifiers (src/analyzer/csharp_analyzer.rs:291-305).
other_facts: The unchanged visitor preserves each namespace on its declarations: src/analyzer/csharp_analyzer.rs:671-685 and 703-707.
The new scanner only scans candidate_files plus the defining file: src/usages/csharp_graph.rs:66-85.
The unchanged candidate provider also includes directory siblings, which can mask the scanner symptom for same-directory files: src/usages/candidates.rs:46-88.
evidence: At intro 88fa9bb729af, both namespace_of_file (src/analyzer/csharp_analyzer.rs:150-159) and the one-namespace admission test (291-305) are additions in the diff. The scanning restriction at src/usages/csharp_graph.rs:66-85 is also new. Thus the decisive loss of namespaces is visible in the diff itself; the unchanged declaration visitor corroborates that a physical file can supply declarations with different namespace values.

defect: Generated-production support checks are introduced only in verify_generated_production, which verify_release_bundle invokes after checksumming the complete bundle and decoding all curated packs and shards. Acquisition verifies before publication, so rejection cannot install the bundle. No elapsed-time claim was verified; attempts are limited to one per canonical catalog per process, so repetition requires a later process or another catalog.

download.rs:208-212 performs synchronous verification before publishing the extracted cache directory.
download.rs:86-91 guards automatic acquisition with claim_catalog_attempt; failure does not imply repeated automatic downloads in the same process for the same canonical catalog.
evidence: Read 3e51cfde577a, its parent diff and fix bd95c2354c20. The diff places the added generated loop after the existing pack loop, but the existing curated decoding at crates/bifrost-semantic-packs/src/release_bundle.rs:1733-1779 is outside its hunks and context. defect: The generation-aware epoch implementation unconditionally begins an Immediate transaction before reading whether stored epochs already match. A cached, read-only epoch lookup therefore waits for an unrelated SQLite writer and can return SQLITE_BUSY even though its matching epoch and generation are readable without a writer reservation.
defect_check: confirmed by static inspection: the matching-epoch branch is reached only after an Immediate transaction succeeds, so it requires the SQLite writer reservation even when no epoch update is needed; no runtime contention test was run.
fact: At src/analyzer/store/mod.rs:4553, ensure_language_epochs_tx starts TransactionBehavior::Immediate before reading the stored epoch at :4556-4562 or taking the unchanged-epoch branch at :4563-4566.
other_facts: src/analyzer/store/mod.rs:4624-4633 reads the current generation with SELECT only; the matching branch does not need to mutate any row.
SQLite Immediate transactions reserve the writer slot even before any UPDATE; this is library behavior, not a hidden repository call chain.
evidence: Read the introducing e21778d1d95 store diff and intro :4549-4586. The new function, Immediate transaction, stored-epoch SELECT, and matching continue branch are all added together in one hunk. The same diff removes the old ensure_language_epoch_tx read-first early return. The misplaced writer reservation is therefore visible in the diff, using ordinary SQLite transaction semantics rather than requiring discovery of an unseen repository writer. Fix 8c91d98583f in crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/store/mod.rs adds a read-only matching fast path before opening the Immediate transaction and a writer-contention regression. The precise timeout outcome was not reproduced.

defect: ProgressReporter::send puts peer.notify_progress inside a 25 ms timeout and drops the send future on expiry. The peer may already have enqueued that notification, so the request can return its response while its notification is still pending; later transport delivery then crosses the request-response boundary and can contaminate the next request stream.
defect_check: not confirmed: the intro proves that a 25 ms timeout abandons the notification wait and the handler returns without a delivery drain, but rmcp enqueue-before-delivery and cancellation behavior cannot be independently verified from the repository at intro. The named fix explicitly describes that dependency behavior.
fact: The notify_progress operation wrapped by ProgressReporter::send (crates/bifrost-mcp/src/rmcp_host.rs:742) must be known to enqueue before waiting for delivery, with dropping its future leaving the queued notification intact; that decisive behavior belongs to external rmcp 3.3.0, identified in Cargo.lock:2523.
other_facts: The timeout expiry is ignored at crates/bifrost-mcp/src/rmcp_host.rs:749.
The synchronous handler awaits execute_tool then immediately arms response timing and returns at crates/bifrost-mcp/src/rmcp_host.rs:2669-2676, without flushing pending notifications.
evidence: Read intro 25bbd98 rmcp_host.rs:739-750, :1546-1577, :2669-2676 and Cargo.lock:2523-2526. The timeout is in the diff; the missing decisive fact is the external peer channel/transport implementation, which is not vendored in this snapshot. Fix 397bcf8 explains enqueue-before-await and adds retained delivery chains plus finish drains, but does not independently establish the dependency implementation at intro.

defect: The new subscript receiver arm calls collection_element_type_fq_name, whose local-array helper treats a write as prior when only its start precedes the read. In $items[copy] = $items[0], resolving the RHS therefore selects that still-in-progress assignment and recursively resolves the identical RHS again, overflowing the native stack and aborting analysis.
defect_check: confirmed by source tracing: a read inside an indexed assignment can select that enclosing unfinished assignment, resolve its RHS, and re-enter the identical subscript inference with the same source position and no recursion bound. The reported native stack overflow was not executed here.

query: Can the new subscript receiver inference reach itself through collection_element_type_fq_name and infer_indexed_local_element_type when the selected indexed write contains the current RHS read?

defect: The new synthetic FileScope spans the entire source and is inserted into the same declaration set used by enclosing_code_unit. A Python module declaration spans the same file, but the unchanged min_by_key(span) chooses arbitrarily between equal spans in the hash-backed set. Choosing FileScope prevents module-scope receiver facts from being found and makes ordinary definition lookups intermittently return no definition.
defect_check: confirmed: the existing Python module and new FileScope both span a normal entire module; the hash-set span-only minimum may select FileScope, for which the Python receiver-facts map has no entry.
fact: Python already registers its real module CodeUnit using the tree root range (src/analyzer/python/adapter.rs:78-84), giving it the same whole-file span as the new synthetic FileScope on the supplied ordinary Python module.
query: What source range does the Python adapter assign to its real module CodeUnit, and can it equal the new FileScope range used by enclosing_code_unit?
other_facts: The intro adds a whole-source FileScope range at src/analyzer/tree_sitter_analyzer.rs:317-333 and retains span-only min_by_key at :1414 over the declaration set.

enclosing_scope_facts uses the selected owner directly as the map key at src/analyzer/usages/python_graph/extractor.rs:286-299, while collect_scope_facts records module facts only for real modules at :736-752.

python_receiver_type_unit depends on those scope facts for an identifier receiver at src/analyzer/usages/get_definition/python.rs:340-353; a variable such as user is not itself a class name for the remaining fallback.
evidence: At intro 8ea28a4, unchanged PythonAdapter::parse_file at adapter.rs:78-84 records the real module using root. Neither adapter.rs nor python_graph/extractor.rs is changed by this commit; the only python/mod.rs change handles FileScope in rendering. The new synthetic full-file range and declaration-set iteration are in the diff, but the pre-existing equal module range is not. Read extractor.rs:298-299,736-752 and get_definition/python.rs:340-353 to confirm the lost receiver facts. Fix 3a7a2ab adds a deterministic preference for real declarations on equal spans.

defect: The new binding-event filter requires a physical declaration range to end before the event becomes visible and returns no candidates if none does. Repeated module assignments share one indexed declaration represented at its final spelling, so an earlier valid binding event loses that declaration and a bare read between assignments incorrectly returns no_indexed_definition.
defect_check: confirmed: repeated assignments replace the same module Field and its declaration range; the new event filter returns an empty list when that surviving range ends after the earlier event.
fact: Repeated module assignments replace one Field CodeUnit and its declaration range with the last assignment, rather than retaining a declaration range for each binding event (crates/bifrost-python/src/declarations.rs:551-569; crates/bifrost-core/src/analyzer/parsed_file.rs:266-275,425).
query: Where do the declaration ranges returned for a repeatedly assigned Python module Field come from, and does replacement preserve earlier assignment ranges?
other_facts: The changed event filter in crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/usages/get_definition/python.rs:1771-1779 accepts only ranges ending at or before event_visible_from and returns no candidates otherwise.
visit_expression_statement permits module assignments at module_control_depth <= 1 (crates/bifrost-python/src/declarations.rs:551), covering a main-guard body.
evidence: At intro 776315a, declarations.rs:551-569 constructs the same module/name Field for successive assignments and calls replace_code_unit. parsed_file.rs:274-275 removes then re-adds it; :425 removes its old declaration ranges. The intro diff changes only get_definition/python.rs and adds tests; neither producer is in that diff. The new helper at python.rs:1759-1797 assumes a range preceding the event. The e9e10f6 fix adds the earliest-range anchor when every recorded declaration follows the event.

defect: New runtime-class mutation guards walk the entire module separately for base/binding queries while charging one shared hierarchy scope budget. A large inert function exhausts that budget across repeated guards, producing incomplete ancestry instead of the complete or inconsistent answer for a tiny hierarchy.
defect_check: confirmed: class_hierarchy shares one bounded session across its base proofs, and each new mutation guard performs a fresh full-module walk. Repeated scans can exhaust ordinary work on unrelated inert syntax. The proposed exact trigger was not executed.
fact: class_hierarchy constructs one ResolutionSession and PythonDefinitionProvider for the whole ancestry traversal (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/python/hierarchy.rs:373), and runtime_source_bases repeatedly calls python_class_object_base_candidate with that same provider for each base (hierarchy.rs:711).
query: Trace class_hierarchy through runtime_source_bases to python_class_object_base_candidate: do successive base proofs reuse the same provider and bounded ResolutionSession?
other_facts: PythonDefinitionProvider::scope_step delegates to its session at crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/usages/get_definition/python.rs:315; ResolutionSession::scope_step charges ScopeNodes at crates/bifrost-core/src/analyzer/usages/resolution_session.rs:196.

The new collector traverses every named module descendant and charges both traversal and classification at crates/bifrost-python/src/source_facts.rs:184; the new runtime guard invokes it on every name at crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/usages/get_definition/python.rs:2093.

evidence: At intro 6ac4593, hierarchy.rs:373-384 creates the shared session/provider; :440-448 passes the same budget into each source owner; :711-725 loops over bases with budget.provider. These lines are outside the intro diff. The changed get_definition/python.rs guard and source_facts.rs:172-214 show the repeated full-tree cost. defect: The intro changes retained fills from independent request-cache domains to one OnceLock-shared domain across sequential fills. JavaFileClassIndexMemo already caches a file-class index even when declaration loading reports StructureUnavailable, but retains neither the gap nor a build receipt. The first fill reports the gap; the second shared-memo hit returns the same empty index without it, allowing an incomplete absence answer to appear complete and be retained.
defect_check: confirmed: the Java file-index memo unconditionally stores the declaration-derived index and returns it directly on hits without replaying incompleteness. Sequential retained fills share that memo after intro, while their ordinary enclosing request has a different domain and cannot supply the first fill gap through inheritance.
fact: JavaSource::unique_class_by_fqn_in_file uses the request-domain JavaFileClassIndexMemo, caches the result of declarations(file) unconditionally, and returns cached indexes without replaying their build gaps at crates/bifrost-jvm-analysis/src/analyzer/java/mod.rs:777-814.
query: Which consumers of the request-cache domain store declaration-derived results without preserving or replaying incomplete-read reasons when a later retained fill reuses the domain?
other_facts: JavaFileClassIndexMemo stores only Arc<JavaFileClassIndex> at java/mod.rs:693-696; the index stores only classes_by_fqn at :660-662.

At intro, crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/tree_sitter_analyzer.rs:17415-17429 returns an empty declaration set when no file state can be obtained, and :10478-10487 records StructureUnavailable for binary or structural-line admission refusal.

An empty class index returns UniqueClassInFile::None at java/mod.rs:685-689.

defect: The new ruby_reference_node climbs from the focused constant through every enclosing scope_resolution before resolving it. In Foo::Bar::Baz, a cursor on Foo or Bar is consequently converted into the whole path and navigates to Baz rather than the selected path segment.
defect_check: confirmed: every focused constant is promoted through all enclosing scope_resolution nodes before resolution, losing the selected segment.
fact: At src/analyzer/usages/get_definition/ruby.rs:106-115, ruby_reference_node unconditionally replaces a focused node with every enclosing scope_resolution, and :41-49 passes that promoted node to constant resolution.
other_facts: At src/analyzer/usages/ruby_graph.rs:298-311, resolve_constant looks up the qualified name of its supplied node; :1075-1085 extracts both scope and terminal name from a scope_resolution.
evidence: Read the new resolver file at cc45d8f092e and its diff. The focused-node selection at :18, constant dispatch at :41-49, ascent loop at :106-113, and forwarding to semantic.resolve_constant at :154-156 all appear in the newly added file. The ascent itself shows why the focused prefix is lost. The existing name-resolution implementation corroborates terminal lookup. Fix e83f3541176 replaces the ascent with a focused-segment helper that only includes the parent when the constant is its terminal name.

defect: rust_role_accepts_current_module now reuses rust_value_namespace_candidate for bare value lookup. That predicate accepts const_item/static_item syntax without excluding impl or trait ownership, replacing the prior parent-class exclusion. Consequently an associated constant under the enclosing type competes with or wins over the module constant for a bare name inside an impl method, although associated constants require an owner-qualified path.
defect_check: confirmed: the new bare-value predicate admits associated const_item declarations; the unchanged enclosing-parent filter permits them inside an impl of that owner, so a module constant can gain an invalid competing candidate.
fact: At src/analyzer/usages/get_definition/rust.rs:880 and :891-894, bare Value lookup uses rust_value_namespace_candidate, whose field test at :938-941 accepts const_item without an ownership check, replacing the former explicit parent-class exclusion.
other_facts: At src/analyzer/usages/get_definition/rust.rs:813-843, current-module lookup collects enclosing owners and allows candidates whose parent is among those owners; this unchanged detail is outside the changed hunk context.
At src/analyzer/rust/declarations.rs:775-783, impl constants are indexed through visit_rust_field with the impl owner as parent; :674-688 records them as Fields.
evidence: Read git show db238908013 for rust.rs and the intro declarations.rs. The hunk changing rust_role_accepts_current_module explicitly removes analyzer.parent_of(candidate).is_none_or(|parent| !parent.is_class()) and replaces it with the new value predicate. The complete new predicate and its const_item/static_item syntax test are also in the diff. Thus the decisive loss of associated-item exclusion is visible without discovering a new caller or value source. The unchanged :840-843 filter and declaration producer corroborate the concrete trigger rather than supply the missing decisive fact. Fix 12f759b2964 introduces rust_declaration_is_module_value_item and excludes impl/trait ownership for bare values.

defect: The initial Rust analyzer visits enum variants as fields and records only the variant itself. Its field visitor never descends into a struct variant field_declaration_list, so named fields inside enum variants disappear from public declaration inventory.
defect_check: confirmed: the initial parser routes enum variants to a leaf field visitor, which records the variant but never visits its named fields.
fact: At src/analyzer/rust_analyzer.rs:478-479, enum_variant is sent to visit_rust_field, whose complete body at :609-650 records one Field and returns without traversing the variant body.
other_facts: src/analyzer/rust_analyzer.rs:80-88 routes enum_item through visit_rust_class_like; :300-301 exposes the resulting declarations through the public analyzer.
evidence: Read the introducing commit 33fba95a5b7 and its new rust_analyzer.rs. The enum dispatch at :472-493 and the entire leaf visitor at :609-650 are additions in the diff, as is the root dispatch at :80-88. There is no missing repository fact: the declaration traversal stops at each enum variant in the code the reviewer sees. Fix c4268c4fdfc adds traversal of the enum_variant body field_declaration_list in crates/bifrost-rust/src/declarations.rs. The reported location numbers differ slightly from the actual intro; these references use the intro.

defect: Lazy Rust reverse-import planning widens exact declaration candidates to every file whose code mentions the terminal module name, then reconstructs forward import edges for all those files. Ordinary variables and other unrelated uses of a common module word enter expensive semantic verification despite having no corresponding import, exhausting interactive usage-search budgets in large workspaces.
defect_check: confirmed: every code mention of the terminal module component enters candidate selection and forward-edge reconstruction before import relevance is checked. The claimed hundreds-of-files timing and budget exhaustion were not reproduced under the no-build/no-test constraint.
fact: The new importer candidate code supplements exact-name files with every code mention of the terminal module name, then reconstructs each candidate file's forward import edges (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/rust/usage_walks.rs:911-938,960-991); the commit message explicitly describes the same widening and verification.
other_facts: The unchanged files_mentioning implementation filters only the occurrence context mask, not import membership (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/rust/usage_queries.rs:381-401).
The intro wires production usage_candidate_files_while through RustUsageWalks and importers_of_seeds_while (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/rust/usage_index.rs:2333-2342).
evidence: At intro 8f0d2a7, the new usage_walks.rs:935-938 adds files_mentioning(last, RUST_OCCURRENCE_CODE), :965-969 resolves forward edges for each declaration candidate, and :986-991 does the same for module candidates. Its commit message, Layer 3, explicitly says candidates include files whose code mentions the target module last component and verification recomputes forward edges. Thus the decisive broadening is already in the reviewer input. Read usage_queries.rs:387-401 to confirm that no structured-import filter is hidden in files_mentioning; fix 6074c79 replaces that supplement with structured module-import candidates.

defect: The new plain_structs prescan ignores unexpanded same-file item macros that can generate impl Drop. Its new S{} proof marks a let-bound local definitely_non_dropping; let_declaration_may_require_drop then reports false and block-exit analysis omits required lexical Drop cleanup uncertainty. This attribution is to the local binding, not a discarded temporary.
defect_check: confirmed: for the supplied unit struct, the prescan has no visible impl_item for the macro-generated destructor, admits S into plain_structs, and marks the let-bound local non-dropping; block cleanup consequently omits its Drop uncertainty.
fact: The new rust_file_facts prescan disqualifies structs only through written impl_item nodes, duplicate declarations and generics, ignores macro invocations, and proves an empty-field struct plain (crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/rust/semantic.rs:4030-4162); all of this logic is added in the diff.
other_facts: The same diff adds the struct_expression plain_structs proof at semantic.rs:1176-1188 and inserts initializer-proven locals into definitely_non_dropping at :771-779.
The existing let_declaration_may_require_drop at semantic.rs:1270-1281 consults that set, and block at :1604-1617 emits lexical cleanup gaps only if a direct let may drop.

The unchanged macro_boundary at semantic.rs:3255-3275 explicitly states that macro token-tree expansion is unavailable; an item macro outside the local procedure does not execute this boundary in that procedure.
evidence: At intro d5c9845, semantic.rs:4106-4130 handles explicit impl_item and otherwise does nothing; :4143-4155 accepts the empty field list. Both the entire prescan and struct-expression proof are new diff hunks, so recognizing that an item macro can supply impl Drop exposes the unsound proof without an additional repository fact. Checked the unchanged local-binding cleanup consumer at :1270-1281 and :1604-1617 to confirm attribution to the let local. The named fix 431089a later removes this file-local plainness proof.

defect: The return-type reader now strips Option<T> to T without requiring an unwrap operation. An ordinary call returning Option<T> is inferred as the payload, so a subsequent bare field read can navigate to a field of T even though the receiver is still an Option.
defect_check: confirmed: an ordinary call uses the shared return-type reader, which now strips Option<T> before resolving its type, without checking for an unwrap operation.
fact: At src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:1054 and :1062-1063, the return-type reader unconditionally unwraps Option, and the ordinary call_expression branch at :1012-1016 uses that reader to infer the call result.
other_facts: At src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:911-915, an unannotated let binding stores the result of rust_value_type_fqn directly as its inferred owner; :600-616 uses the inferred receiver owner for member lookup.
evidence: Read git show 309939da522 and the intro file. The return-type-reader hunk shows unconditional rust_unwrap_container_type(return_type).or(Some(return_type)) and newly adds Option prefixes to that helper. The ordinary call branch at :1012-1016 is also changed and visible, so no unseen caller is required to see that direct calls receive the payload type. Fix 36fa96bd75c changes the return reader to Some(return_type) and moves unwrapping to syntax-specific operations.

defect: The let-condition activation change asks both if_expression and while_expression for their consequence field. The Rust grammar gives while_expression a body field instead, so rust_binding_activation returns None for while-let pattern binders and drops their structural binding facts.
defect_check: confirmed by static source comparison and the fixing grammar-boundary regression: the added consequence-only lookup returns None for the while_expression body shape, causing the structural environment to omit the binder. No parser or test was executed here.
fact: The external Rust Tree-sitter contract gives while_expression a body field rather than consequence, but crates/bifrost-rust/src/structural.rs:424-427 at intro requests consequence for both loop and if owners.
other_facts: Existing Rust consumers already allow body as well as consequence: crates/bifrost-rust/src/lexical_scope.rs:1085-1091 and crates/bifrost-rust/src/resolution.rs:7637-7643.
crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/structural/lexical_environment.rs:628-635 records BindingActivationUnknown and skips the binding when binding_activation returns None.
evidence: Read eea67f995994 and its parent diff. The owner alternatives and new consequence lookup at crates/bifrost-rust/src/structural.rs:424-427 are visible in the diff; the decisive missing information is the third-party grammar field contract, not a caller identity or an execution route. Existing intro readers at lexical_scope.rs:1085-1091 and resolution.rs:7637-7643 corroborate the separate body shape but do not define the grammar. Fix 8d85c2acd917 selects body for while_expression and adds a grammar-boundary regression asserting this shape. The grammar implementation itself was not available as tracked source in the inspected snapshot, so that part of confirmation relies on the existing consumers and supplied fix rather than an executed parse.

defect: The new concrete-callee discharge reads Some(empty) from virtual_dispatch_implementor_targets as a proven absence of workspace overrides. That existing helper returns Some(empty) for an unproven member family too, so unresolved or truncated hierarchy evidence can now close the dynamic-dispatch gap and falsely certify the concrete call as complete.
defect_check: confirmed: the existing helper returns Some(empty) for any unproven member family; the new concrete branch reads that value as proven absence and allows the dynamic-dispatch gap to discharge. Java can reach an unproven family by exhausting the shared visit budget at intro.
fact: virtual_dispatch_implementor_targets returns Some(Vec::new()) when answer.is_proven() is false, at crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/semantic/workspace_oracle/dispatch.rs:941-970, so an empty result does not prove that no override exists.
query: What return values can virtual_dispatch_implementor_targets produce for incomplete or unsupported member-family answers, and can Some(empty) mean anything besides proven absence?
other_facts: The new concrete branch at dispatch.rs:549-558 leaves concrete_overrides_proven_absent true on Some(empty), which the new discharge predicate consumes.
